summary.title: Clang Compiler User's Manual
summary.one_liner: Reference for using Clang as an end-user compiler: supported languages, diagnostic-formatting and warning flags, crash-reproducer options, and optimization-report flags.
takeaways: Clang supports C, Objective-C, C++, Objective-C++ and OpenCL C dialects, and aims for GCC driver compatibility; clang-cl targets cl.exe compatibility.
Warning and error control is set with flags such as -Werror, -Werror=foo, -Wfoo, -Wno-foo, -w, -Weverything and -pedantic.
Diagnostic output can be tailored with options for column numbers, caret lines, colors, output format (clang, msvc, vi, sarif) and hotness info.
Crash diagnostics produce preprocessed source and run scripts; -gen-reproducer creates them without a crash.
Optimization reports (-fsave-optimization-record, -foptimization-record-file, -foptimization-record-passes) record which transformations were made or missed.
summary.summary: This is the official Clang user manual, aimed at people using Clang as a compiler rather than building tools on it. It starts with an overview of supported language standards (C through C2y, C++98 through C++29, OpenCL) and a glossary of compiler terms such as lexer, parser, Sema, frontend and backend. The bulk of the page is a reference of command-line options, grouped under error and warning control, diagnostic formatting, crash reporting, and optimization reports, each with short examples of the output. The page excerpt ends mid-section, so target-specific and floating-point details are not covered here.
